cases.title: choose(*xs): int → str
cases.summary: Permitting the zero-parameter candidate changes overload selection, not only diagnostics.
cases.runtimeNote: Both results are possible. The baseline’s int was already incomplete for an empty list; the PR’s str is incomplete for a singleton.
steps: An unknown-length list reaches two overloads.
We trace the zero-parameter candidate here. The one-int candidate separately matches the same splat.
The zero-candidate sees Star([], int, []).
Its local data is the same as case ①. The baseline comment explicitly mentioned avoiding zero-arity overload swallowing.
The zero-candidate cannot set matched=true.
The one-int candidate can set matched=true and was already accepted before this PR.
The zero-candidate now survives argument checking.
Before its extra-argument error eliminated it. After it adds no call error, so both candidates can proceed.
The inferred return type changes from int to str.
In default overload mode this example chooses the first surviving candidate. The PR therefore changes a downstream inference policy as well as arity diagnostics.
cases.outcome: This is an important intentional-policy question, not a standalone proof that only the PR is unsound. Add a return-type test and decide what uncertain arity should mean for overloaded calls.
cases.lessonTitle: A diagnostic also acts as candidate-filter data.
cases.lesson: extra_positional_args feeds call_errors. Overload matching uses call_errors to eliminate candidates; removing an error can change the selected return type.

lineNotes.1472: This false is the match-arm value assigned to extra_arg, not a function return. It skips the append to extra_positional_args; the loop then breaks and remaining argument/keyword analysis continues.
lineNotes.1474: Gradual middle=Any still bypasses arity rejection, as it did before this PR.
lineNotes.1480: One source range is pushed, not one range per runtime element. That is where the baseline’s diagnostic “got 1” comes from.
lineNotes.588: The fallback unions produced element types and replaces both fixed ends with []. Different possible lengths are not retained.
lineNotes.691: History changes to true only after a positional match. For zero-parameter calls this line is never reached.
lineNotes.688: Increment only while there is a fixed prefix element at this cursor; no suffix element is removed.
lineNotes.2291: The downstream error emitter counts extra source ranges. A change here also affects overload candidate elimination.
lineNotes.2883: callable_infer_inner returns ArgMap beside the inferred Python result type, not instead of it. Overload matching retains this map as candidate metadata.
lineNotes.2712: This caller receives ArgMap while callable_infer_params reports diagnostics through the error collectors passed by reference.
lineNotes.1311: The while loop belongs to one source argument. A Star stays available after a finite positional match; an empty parameter stack brings it to the None branch.
